data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Nehaniel means 'God is gracious'. This name can be found in the Old Testament as the name of an angel mentioned in Daniel 9:21. The name is also associated with the early Christian martyr Saint Nehan, who is venerated in the Eastern Orthodox Church. The name Nehaniel carries the meaning “God is gracious” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Nehaniel usually hope their child will grow to embody god is gracious and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the graciousness of God towards humanity.
data.etymology: Nehaniel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God is gracious.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nehaniel total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: נחניאל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם נחניאל מאוחד מהמילים 'נח' (נחל) ו'חניאל' (אדם חזק). השם עוצב במקור לתאר אדם שאינו תלוי באחרים, כמו הצומח שגדל בוודאי. בספר ישעיהו (7:23), נחניאל הוא שבט של ישראל. השם עוצב גם לתאר אדם שאינו תלוי בתקופה, כמו העץ הנותן פרי לאורך השנים. במובן זה, השם נחניאל מעמדד עם הערכים הנוצריים של ראש, חזק, ובלתי תלוי

in_greek.name: Νεχαniήλ
in_greek.long_meaning: ὁ ὄνομα Νεχαniήλ συνίσταται ἐκ τῶν ῥημάτων Νε- (Νε-χ-αλ) καὶ Χανιήλ (ἀνήρ ἰσχυρός). ἐν τῇ εἰκόνα τοῦ λειμῶνος, ὁ Νεχαniήλ εἶναι ἄνθρωπος πλήρης ἰσχύος, οὐχ ὑπὸ τίς ἁλώσει. ἐν τῇ εἰκόνα τοῦ δένδρου, ὁ Νεχαniήλ εἶναι ἄνθρωπος πλήρης ἀγάπης, ὃς δίδωσιν φρούτα εἰς πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας. ἐν τῇ εἰκόνα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ὁ Νεχαniήλ εἶναι ἄνθρωπος πλήρης χαρᾶς, ὃς δίδωσιν φαῦλα εἰς πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας

in_latin.name: Nehaniel
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Nehaniel ex radicibus N- (Nech-al) et Chaniel (vir fortis) formatur. In imagine viti, Nehaniel significat virum fortissimum, qui non est in vinculis. In imagine arboris, Nehaniel significat virum qui dat fructus in omni die. In imagine Dei, Nehaniel significat virum qui dat gratiam in omni die

in_english.name: Nehaniel
in_english.long_meaning: The name Nehaniel is derived from the Hebrew words 'Nech' (watering) and 'Chaniel' (strong man). In the biblical context, Nehaniel is associated with the tribe of Israel. The name is also a metaphor for a person who is not dependent on external factors, much like a plant that grows independently. In this sense, the name Nehaniel aligns with Christian values of strength, independence, and self-reliance. In modern times, the name Nehaniel is often given to parents seeking a strong and independent child

data.cultural_impact: The name Nehaniel has cultural significance as it comes from the Hebrew language and adds a biblical connection to the name. It was used for an angel in the Old Testament, and its use in the Eastern Orthodox Church for a martyr further cements its place in Christian history. The name may appeal to those who value biblical roots and ancient traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: Nehaniel is a name that represents God's grace and goodness. It is a reminder that God is merciful and compassionate towards us. The name can serve as a source of and encouragement in times of hardship or adversity. It can also be a daily reminder of the grace and love that God extends to us each day.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nehaniel: "Comforter of God," suggesting a deep connection to divine consolation and healing. The name embodies the soothing presence of the divine in moments of sorrow and loss.

biblical_reference.note: Nehaniel is mentioned as a tribe of Israel in Isaiah 7:23

historical_references.reference: The Book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish text believed to have been written between the 2nd century BC and the 1st century AD, mentions a fallen angel named Nehaniel who took human wives and fathered the giants known as the Nephilim.

Irenaeus of Lyons, an early Christian theologian and bishop, in his work 'Against Heresies' written around 180 AD, lists Nehaniel as one of the leaders of the fallen angels and demons who seduced women and produced the Nephilim.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name 'Nehaniel' is often seen in modern contexts related to New Age spirituality, Angelic Reiki, and alternative medicine. Nehaniel is frequently invoked as an archangel in various spiritual practices and energy healing modalities. On Facebook groups, blogs, and websites, you can find discussions about Nehaniel's role in ascended master teachings and his influence on personal growth and transformational processes. In metaphysical bookstores, you may find books, cards, and crystals dedicated to Nehaniel's energy and teachings.
